exposure: duration of second stage of labor
Duration of second stage of labor
Duration of second stage of labor (<1 hour, 1-2 hours, 2-3 hours, >3 hours)
outcome: Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal delivery, operative vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery)
Maternal morbidity (third- or fourth-degree tear, postpartum hemorrhage)
Neonatal birth injury (cephalohematoma, fetal laceration, brachial plexus palsy, facial nerve palsy, fetal fracture)
finding: Increasing duration of the second stage of labor was associated with increased rates of operative vaginal and cesarean delivery, as well as increased maternal morbidity (third- or fourth-degree tear, postpartum hemorrhage) and neonatal birth injury.
mod_finding: The rate of operative vaginal delivery increased with increasing duration of second stage labor, while the rate of spontaneous vaginal delivery decreased.
